findings.title: Broken hash primitive (MD5/SHA-1) — lib/insecurity.ts:41
findings.scenario: MD5/SHA-1 are collision-broken; used for passwords they are trivially cracked, and for integrity of attacker-influenced data they are forgeable.
findings.recommended_mitigation_title: Use SHA-256+ for integrity and a password KDF (argon2id / bcrypt / scrypt) for credentials.

findings.title: express-jwt middleware missing algorithms allowlist — lib/insecurity.ts:53
findings.scenario: Without an algorithm allowlist the token middleware that guards every authenticated route accepts tokens an attacker signs with a weaker or unintended algorithm, so a forged token passes as any user on every protected route.
findings.recommended_mitigation_title: Add `algorithms: ['RS256']` (or matching) to the expressJwt() options object.

findings.title: Non-cryptographic RNG for a secret/token — lib/insecurity.ts:53
findings.scenario: A predictable token/secret lets an attacker guess or brute-force session identifiers, reset links, or OTPs.
findings.recommended_mitigation_title: Use crypto.randomBytes / crypto.randomUUID / webcrypto getRandomValues for any security value.

findings.title: JWT decode used without signature verification — lib/insecurity.ts:56
findings.scenario: Decode-only flows let an attacker construct a token with any claims (admin, sub=victim, scope=*) — no key material required.
findings.recommended_mitigation_title: Replace `.decode(token)` with `.verify(token, key, { algorithms: [...] })` and gate authorization on the verified payload only.

findings.title: JWT verify call missing algorithms allowlist (algorithm confusion) — lib/insecurity.ts:189
findings.scenario: Without an explicit algorithm allowlist, attackers can forge tokens with alg:none (older lib versions) or use the public key as an HMAC secret to mint valid signatures.
findings.recommended_mitigation_title: Always pass `algorithms: ['RS256']` (or the project's chosen alg) as the third argument's options object to jwt.verify.

findings.title: Broken authorization — attacker-controlled owner ID in resource query — routes/address.ts:11
findings.scenario: A signed-in attacker puts another user's ID into the owner field of the request (req.body.UserId and the like); the query trusts it instead of the session identity, so the attacker reads or changes every other user's records — horizontal privilege escalation across all accounts.
findings.recommended_mitigation_title: Replace req.body.UserId/userId/ownerId with req.user.id (or equivalent session-derived identity) in every WHERE/filter clause.

findings.recommended_mitigation_title: Add an explicit auth middleware (isAuthorized() / passport.authenticate() / requireAuth) to the route registration, or mark the route intentionally public via app.get(...) for read-only access only.
